pillar_b_first_principles_investigation.root_cause_summary:
1. Backdoor Identifiability of OLS in W15_corr_vs_cause & W15_obs_confounder (P15-H1): Because all variables in W15_corr_vs_cause and W15_obs_confounder are observed with independent noise (epsilon ~ N(0, 0.05^2)), conditioning on all observed covariates in OLS (observational_linear) automatically blocks the observed backdoor path via Frisch-Waugh-Lovell partial regression, scoring ~0.003 nRMSE. By contrast, observational_mlp (with L2 weight decay) splits weight across collinear features (0.086 and 0.137), and observational_linear collapses completely when a confounder is unobserved (W15_hidden_confounder: 0.604) or under multi-cause collinearity (W15_multi_cause: 0.210).
2. Equal Interventional Data Ceiling & Discarded Observational Data (P15-H5 & P15-H6): In the initial confirmatory run, causal_intervention discarded all passive observational data and trained only on N_int=480 interventional samples—the exact same dataset given to mlp_intervention—so both saturated at F1=1.000 and ate_nmae had a 0.013 floor.
pillar_b_first_principles_investigation.first_principles_solution: Implemented Joint Invariant Causal Fusion (CausalStructuralModel.fit_joint_causal_structure): uses scarce/controlled interventions to discover unconfounded Pa(Y), runs a Chow-type coefficient invariance test (z_diff < 2.5) between interventional and observational regressions on Pa(Y), and pools obs + int on the invariant causal subset.
